title: Kediri Kingdom
capsule: Kediri was a Hindu-Buddhist Javanese kingdom centred on Dahanapura in East Java, ruling from roughly 1042 to 1222. It rose after the partition of the Mataram kingdom between Airlangga's two sons and became one of the most productive eras of Old Javanese literature, producing major kakawin epics such as Mpu Sedah and Mpu Panuluh's Bharatayuddha (1157) under King Jayabaya. The kingdom controlled rice-surplus hinterlands and access to East Java's maritime trade routes, exporting pepper and luxury goods. It ended abruptly in 1222 when Ken Arok, a vassal lord of Tumapel, defeated King Kertajaya at the Battle of Ganter and founded the Singhasari kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Kediri's territorial extent is inferred primarily from epigraphy and later Javanese chronicles; direct archaeological evidence for its boundaries is sparse, making precise borders uncertain.
